note: Complete public scientific-checker bank. Inactive unless SCIBENCH_TRIGGER_LOG is set. Historical quality-review metadata does not remove checker IDs from the agent-visible task.

checkers.alarm: the reversed-input profile, reversed back, differs beyond 1e-9
checkers.invariant: the scale profile is equivariant under sequence reversal: protein_scale(reverse(s))[::-1] == protein_scale(s)
checkers.observation_point: after the scale loop; the checker re-calls protein_scale() on the reversed sequence
checkers.precondition: a valid standard protein sequence whose residues are all in the scale dict, an even positive window, 0 <= edge <= 1
checkers.rationale: the window weights are meant to be applied symmetrically, but the middle-residue index the loop uses is off-centre for even windows

checkers.alarm: a higher pH yields a greater net charge beyond 1e-9
checkers.invariant: net charge is monotonically non-increasing as pH rises
checkers.observation_point: in isoelectric_point(); the checker sweeps charge_at_pH over a 0.25-pH grid
checkers.precondition: a non-empty valid protein sequence and finite pH values in [0, 14]
checkers.rationale: Henderson-Hasselbalch partial charges are individually monotone in pH; the sum must be too

checkers.alarm: the all-A Tm exceeds this sequence's Tm, or exceeds the all-G Tm, beyond 1e-6
checkers.invariant: at fixed length, raising %GC does not lower Tm_GC (empirical B > 0)
checkers.observation_point: before returning melting_temp; the checker calls Tm_GC on all-A and all-G sequences of the same length
checkers.precondition: an unambiguous DNA sequence of length >= 4. Built-in value sets 1-8 all have empirical GC coefficient B > 0; a caller-supplied userset with B <= 0 inverts the premise and is excluded.
checkers.rationale: every published Tm_GC value set has a positive %GC coefficient

checkers.alarm: the two temperatures differ beyond 1e-6
checkers.invariant: Tm_NN(seq) == Tm_NN(reverse_complement(seq)) with every other argument identical
checkers.observation_point: before returning melting_temp; the checker re-calls Tm_NN on the reverse complement with the same salt parameters
checkers.precondition: DNA primer (>=2 nt, ACGT/U), c_seq/shift/selfcomp/custom nn_table unset; re-call forwards every result-affecting Tm_NN arg incl. dnac1/dnac2.
checkers.rationale: a perfect duplex has the same nearest-neighbor stack set read from either strand

checkers.alarm: the doubled-[Na+] Tm is below this Tm, or this Tm is below the halved-[Na+] Tm, beyond 1e-6
checkers.invariant: raising [Na+] does not lower Tm_NN
checkers.observation_point: before returning melting_temp; the checker re-calls Tm_NN at half and double [Na+]
checkers.precondition: DNA primer (>=2 nt, ACGT/U), default nn_table (caller did not pass a non-default table), saltcorr 1-4, K/Tris/Mg/dNTPs unset, Na>0; re-call forwards dnac1/dnac2 and nn_table, varies only [Na+].
checkers.rationale: counter-ions screen backbone charge and stabilise the duplex; every salt-correction method 1-4 is increasing in log[Na+]

checkers.alarm: corr is not between the half- and double-[Na+] values, or the 1 M value is not 0
checkers.invariant: the term is k * log10([Na+] in M): monotonically increasing in [Na+] and exactly 0 at [Na+] = 1 M
checkers.observation_point: before returning corr; the checker re-calls salt_correction at half [Na+], double [Na+], and 1 M
checkers.precondition: method in {1, 3, 4}, only Na set (K=Tris=Mg=dNTPs=0), Na > 0
checkers.rationale: methods 1/3/4 are pure logarithms of ionic strength; method 2 has a saturation term and is intentionally excluded

checkers.alarm: any window's complement skew is not the negation of the original beyond 1e-9
checkers.invariant: GC_skew(complement(seq)) is the element-wise negation of GC_skew(seq)
checkers.observation_point: before returning; the checker re-calls GC_skew on the (non-reversed) complement
checkers.precondition: an unambiguous DNA sequence and a positive window
checkers.rationale: complementing swaps G and C counts in every window, flipping the sign of G - C

checkers.alarm: the two masses differ beyond 1e-6
checkers.invariant: the mass is invariant under residue permutation
checkers.observation_point: after computing the mass; the checker re-calls molecular_weight on the reversed sequence
checkers.precondition: a valid protein sequence of length >= 2; the second call uses the same monoisotopic flag
checkers.rationale: mass is a composition sum minus (n - 1) condensation waters, independent of order

checkers.alarm: the RNA mass is not greater than the DNA mass
checkers.invariant: the RNA mass exceeds the mass of the corresponding DNA string (U to T)
checkers.observation_point: after the mass calculation; the checker re-calls molecular_weight on the T-substituted string as DNA
checkers.precondition: an unambiguous single-stranded linear sequence of A/C/G/U, evaluated as RNA
checkers.rationale: per residue the ribose ring adds a 2'-oxygen that outweighs the thymine 5-methyl lost when T becomes U, so RNA of a given base string is heavier than the DNA of the same string

checkers.alarm: the two angles differ beyond 1e-9
checkers.invariant: calc_angle(v1, v2, v3) == calc_angle(v3, v2, v1)
checkers.observation_point: before returning; the checker re-calls calc_angle with the endpoints swapped
checkers.precondition: three distinct Vector points
checkers.rationale: the angle at a vertex does not depend on which arm is named first

checkers.alarm: the transformed angle differs beyond 1e-7
checkers.invariant: the angle is unchanged by applying one rigid rotation plus translation to all three points
checkers.observation_point: before returning; the checker re-computes calc_angle on the transformed points
checkers.precondition: three finite Vector points with |coordinate| < 1e6, pairwise separated by at least ~1e-6 of the coordinate scale; the bound keeps the checker's quadratic norm and rigid-transform arithmetic inside its float64 error model.
checkers.rationale: bond angles are Euclidean invariants

checkers.alarm: the transformed dihedral differs beyond 1e-7
checkers.invariant: the dihedral is unchanged by one rigid rotation plus translation of all four points
checkers.observation_point: before returning; the checker re-computes calc_dihedral on the transformed points
checkers.precondition: four Vector points, pairwise separated by at least ~1e-6 of the coordinate scale (below that the rigid-motion probe's own arithmetic loses the geometry).
checkers.rationale: torsion angles are invariant under proper rigid motions

checkers.alarm: the mirrored dihedral is not the negation of the original beyond 1e-7 (and the angle is not +/- pi)
checkers.invariant: reflecting all four points (z -> -z) negates the signed dihedral
checkers.observation_point: before returning; the checker re-computes calc_dihedral on the mirrored points
checkers.precondition: four points with non-degenerate bonds and |dihedral| not equal to pi
checkers.rationale: a torsion angle is a pseudoscalar; an improper transformation flips its sign

checkers.alarm: R @ R.T is not the identity, or det(R) != 1, beyond 1e-9
checkers.invariant: rotmat(p, q) is orthogonal with determinant +1
checkers.observation_point: before returning the matrix
checkers.precondition: two non-zero, non-collinear Vectors p, q (the antiparallel case p = -k q is a documented rotmat singularity and is excluded)
checkers.rationale: a proper rotation preserves lengths and orientation

checkers.alarm: the rotated p is not parallel to q, or its norm changed, beyond 1e-7
checkers.invariant: p.left_multiply(rotmat(p, q)) points along q and has the same norm as p
checkers.observation_point: before returning the matrix
checkers.precondition: two finite non-zero, non-collinear Vectors p, q with |coordinate| < 1e6; the bound keeps quadratic norm/dot-product arithmetic representable
checkers.rationale: rotmat is documented to rotate p onto q

checkers.invariant: the rotation returned by the SVD superposition is a proper rotation: R^T R = I and det(R) = +1
checkers.observation_point: after SVDSuperimposer.run(), before Superimposer.set_atoms returns
checkers.precondition: two equal-length lists of >=3 atoms whose coordinates are not all collinear
checkers.rationale: a reflection (det -1) superposes mirror-image structures and would make an enantiomer look identical to its mirror

checkers.alarm: |rms(fixed, rigid(moving)) - rms(fixed, moving)| > 1e-6
checkers.invariant: the optimal-superposition RMSD is unchanged when the moving coordinates are first transformed by an arbitrary rigid motion
checkers.observation_point: after SVDSuperimposer.run(), before set_atoms returns
checkers.precondition: two equal-length, non-collinear atom lists
checkers.rationale: the least-squares superposition distance is an intrinsic property of the two shapes and cannot depend on their initial placement

checkers.alarm: |rms(moving, fixed) - rms(fixed, moving)| > 1e-6 * max(1, rms)
checkers.invariant: the optimal-superposition RMSD is symmetric in its two arguments: rms(A, B) = rms(B, A)
checkers.observation_point: after SVDSuperimposer.run(), before set_atoms returns
checkers.precondition: two equal-length, non-collinear atom lists
checkers.rationale: superposition RMSD is a metric on conformations; asymmetry means the centroid or normalisation handling differs between the two roles

checkers.alarm: rms(fixed, rigid(fixed)) > 1e-4
checkers.invariant: the optimal-superposition RMSD is 0
checkers.observation_point: after SVDSuperimposer.run(), before set_atoms returns
checkers.precondition: the moving atom list is an exact rigid image of the fixed atom list (>=3 non-collinear atoms)
checkers.rationale: two structures that are congruent by a rigid motion must be superposable to zero; a non-zero result means the algorithm missed a known exact solution (e.g. the SVD sign branch)

checkers.alarm: |rms(P.fixed, P.moving) - rms(fixed, moving)| > 1e-6
checkers.invariant: applying the same row permutation to both atom lists leaves the optimal-superposition RMSD unchanged
checkers.observation_point: after SVDSuperimposer.run(), before set_atoms returns
checkers.precondition: two equal-length, non-collinear atom lists
checkers.rationale: RMSD sums over paired points; a dependence on enumeration order means an index-order assumption has leaked into the computation

checkers.alarm: |score(B, A) - score(A, B)| > 1e-9 (relative)
checkers.invariant: score(A, B) = score(B, A)
checkers.observation_point: after PairwiseAligner.score computes the score, before it returns
checkers.precondition: mode='global'; a symmetric scoring scheme; two non-empty sequences; every score term exceeds traceback epsilon and max_term*max_sequence_length is below float64 overflow with a factor-16 safety margin
checkers.rationale: under a symmetric scoring model the optimal alignment score is a symmetric function of the sequence pair; asymmetry means target/query gap or matrix indexing is not even-handed and homology calls depend on argument order

checkers.alarm: |score(A, B) - align(A, B).score| > 1e-9 (relative)
checkers.invariant: the score reported by score() equals the score of the best alignment returned by align()
checkers.observation_point: after PairwiseAligner.align builds the alignments, before returning
checkers.precondition: two non-empty sequences expressible as text; any scoring scheme whose nonzero terms exceed traceback epsilon and whose max_term*max_sequence_length is below float64 overflow with a factor-16 safety margin; any mode
checkers.rationale: the score-only dynamic program and the traceback share an optimum by construction; a discrepancy means one of the two recurrences is wrong

checkers.alarm: |score(A[::-1], B[::-1]) - score(A, B)| > 1e-9 (relative)
checkers.invariant: score(A, B) = score(reverse(A), reverse(B))
checkers.observation_point: after PairwiseAligner.score computes the score, before it returns
checkers.precondition: mode='global'; symmetric scoring scheme; left-end and right-end gap scores equal; two non-empty sequences; representable DP-intermediate bound as in BP-ALN-001
checkers.rationale: reversing both sequences transposes the dynamic-programming matrix; a change in the global score means the left/right boundary gap handling is asymmetric

checkers.alarm: |score_with(M^T) - score_with(M)| > 1e-9 (relative)
checkers.invariant: replacing the substitution matrix with its transpose does not change the score
checkers.observation_point: after PairwiseAligner.score computes the score, before it returns
checkers.precondition: mode='global'; a symmetric substitution matrix is set; equal target/query gap scores; two non-empty sequences; representable DP-intermediate bound as in BP-ALN-001
checkers.rationale: for a symmetric substitution model the matrix transpose is the identity operation; a difference means the aligner indexes the matrix as M[a][b] where it should use M[b][a] (or vice versa)

checkers.alarm: additive input and any leaf-pair patristic distance differs by > tol between the tree and the tree built from a row/col-permuted copy, tol = max(1e-9, 64*eps(entry dtype)) * max(1, largest finite pairwise distance)
checkers.invariant: for additive input, permuting the rows/columns of the matrix yields a tree with identical patristic distances between every pair of leaves
checkers.observation_point: after nj() builds the tree, before returning
checkers.precondition: an additive finite DistanceMatrix with >=4 taxa whose max distance is <= float_max/(64*n), so NJ row sums and affine updates are representable; non-additive input is out of scope
checkers.rationale: for additive data NJ reconstructs the unique generating tree; an order dependence then means the join sequence is decided by an implementation artefact rather than the data

checkers.alarm: additive input and an output patristic distance differs from the input distance by > tol, tol = max(1e-9, 64*eps(entry dtype)) * max(1, largest finite pairwise distance)
checkers.invariant: for additive input, NJ reconstructs the generating tree exactly: every output patristic distance equals the corresponding input distance
checkers.observation_point: after nj() builds the tree, before returning
checkers.precondition: additive finite DistanceMatrix with n>=4 and max distance <= float_max/(64*n), decided by the exact four-point condition plus triangle inequality
checkers.rationale: exact reconstruction on additive data is the correctness theorem for NJ (Saitou-Nei 1987; Studier-Keppler 1988); a deviation means NJ failed on an input it provably handles

checkers.alarm: a root-to-leaf depth differs by > tol, or the two largest of a leaf triple's pairwise patristic distances differ by > tol, tol = max(1e-9, 64*eps(entry dtype)) * max(1, largest finite pairwise distance)
checkers.invariant: the tree is ultrametric: all leaves equidistant from the root, and for any three leaves the two largest pairwise patristic distances are equal (three-point condition)
checkers.observation_point: after upgma() builds the tree, before returning
checkers.precondition: a finite DistanceMatrix with >=3 taxa and max distance <= float_max/(64*n), so UPGMA averages and branch arithmetic are representable
checkers.rationale: UPGMA assumes a molecular clock; a non-ultrametric result cannot be read as a clock-like divergence history, which is the modelling premise of the method

checkers.alarm: min branch length < -tol, tol = max(1e-9, 64*eps(entry dtype)) * max(1, largest finite pairwise distance)
checkers.invariant: every estimated branch length is >= 0
checkers.observation_point: after the tree is built, before returning
checkers.precondition: UPGMA on a valid finite matrix, or NJ on an additive finite matrix, with max distance <= float_max/(64*n); NJ negative branches on non-additive input are out of scope
checkers.rationale: a negative branch length is negative evolutionary change; it has no biological meaning and corrupts every length-weighted downstream analysis (patristic distance, rate and date estimation, ancestral reconstruction)
checkers.scientific_quantity: estimated branch length (expected substitutions per site)

checkers.alarm: |C-computed score - column-wise sum| > 1e-3 (relative)
checkers.invariant: the site score equals the sum of the per-position log-odds entries pssm[seq[i]][i]
checkers.observation_point: after _pwm.calculate fills the score array, before calculate() returns
checkers.precondition: a DNA PSSM (ACGT); a sequence at least as long as the motif with only ACGT; score at offset 0
checkers.rationale: positional independence (a sum of per-column log-odds) is the defining assumption of the PSSM model; the C routine and a direct sum are independent implementations of it and a mismatch means the reported score is not the model log-odds

checkers.alarm: a returned score is < pssm.min - 1e-6 or > pssm.max + 1e-6
checkers.invariant: every site score lies in [pssm.min, pssm.max]
checkers.observation_point: after _pwm.calculate fills the score array, before calculate() returns
checkers.precondition: a DNA PSSM; any ACGT query sequence; pssm.min and pssm.max finite
checkers.rationale: pssm.max is the consensus score and pssm.min the anticonsensus score; threshold-based motif search and score-to-p-value mapping rely on these bounds, so a score outside them cannot be placed on the motif's score distribution

checkers.alarm: |forward score - reverse-complement score| > 1e-3 (relative)
checkers.invariant: score(S) with the PSSM equals score(reverse-complement(S)) with reverse_complement(PSSM)
checkers.observation_point: after _pwm.calculate fills the score array, before calculate() returns
checkers.precondition: a DNA PSSM; a query sequence exactly the motif length with only ACGT
checkers.rationale: a binding site can occur on either strand; the forward and reverse-complement scorings describe the same physical binding event, so an asymmetry biases every both-strands genome scan by strand

checkers.alarm: |18.0153 - (2*atom_weights["H"] + atom_weights["O"])| > 5e-4
checkers.invariant: the hard-coded average condensation water 18.0153 equals 2*H + O from IUPACData.atom_weights (the standard atomic-weight table used elsewhere in Biopython)
checkers.observation_point: entry of molecular_weight, before the residue sum
checkers.precondition: the average-mass path of molecular_weight (monoisotopic=False); any call
checkers.rationale: a formula constant that disagrees with the module's own element table silently biases every molecular weight by a fixed offset per residue

checkers.alarm: max(abs(rot @ rot.T - I)) or abs(det(rot)-1) exceeds tol = max(1e-8, 64*eps(coarsest input/rot float dtype)) (float64 1e-8, float32 ~7.6e-6)
checkers.invariant: the rotation matrix rot returned by QCPSuperimposer.run is a proper rotation: it is orthogonal (rot @ rot.T == I) and orientation-preserving (det(rot) == +1)
checkers.observation_point: in QCPSuperimposer.run, immediately after self.rot is assigned from qcp(...)
checkers.precondition: any two point sets of equal size N >= 3 with matching shape (Nx3), each not all-collinear and not all-coincident with its own centroid
checkers.rationale: QCP is an eigen-decomposition method that must return a proper rotation; any departure from orthogonality or det=+1 means the transform is not a physically valid rigid motion

checkers.alarm: self.get_rms() > self.get_init_rms() + tol, where tol = max(1e-6*scale, max(1e-3, 16*sqrt(eps))*max(scale, radius)), scale = max(1, get_init_rms(), get_rms()), radius = max over the two sets of the RMS distance of the (centred) coordinates from the origin, eps = machine epsilon of the coarsest input float dtype
checkers.invariant: get_rms() after the optimal rotation/translation is applied is <= get_init_rms(), because QCP minimizes RMSD over all rigid motions and the identity motion is one member of that search space
checkers.observation_point: in QCPSuperimposer.run, after self.rms is assigned and get_init_rms() can be computed from stored coords
checkers.precondition: any two point sets of equal size N >= 1 with matching shape (Nx3) for which set_atoms/set + run have been successfully called
checkers.rationale: if the algorithm's own reported minimum RMSD exceeds the RMSD of doing nothing, the returned fit is not actually optimal, undermining every downstream use of it as a best-fit superposition
checkers.scientific_quantity: minimized RMSD of the optimal rigid superposition

checkers.alarm: abs(get_rms() - sqrt(mean(sum((reference_coords - get_transformed())**2, axis=1)))) > tol, tol = max(max(1e-3, 32*sqrt(eps))*radius, 64*eps*max|coord|), radius = RMS distance of reference_coords from their centroid, eps = machine epsilon of the coarsest input float dtype
checkers.invariant: the scalar RMSD from get_rms() (computed algebraically via the QCP eigenvalue) must agree with the RMSD computed directly from Euclidean distances between reference_coords and get_transformed()
checkers.observation_point: in QCPSuperimposer.run, after self.rot/self.tran are set
checkers.precondition: any two point sets of equal size N >= 1 with matching shape (Nx3) for which run() completes (rot, tran defined)
checkers.rationale: QCP's headline RMSD is obtained algebraically, never by actually moving points; disagreement with the RMSD from literally applying rot/tran means at least one of rot, tran, rms is wrong relative to the others
checkers.scientific_quantity: RMSD of the fitted superposition, computed via two independent representations

checkers.alarm: with s = max(1, max|coord|) and t = (s,s,s): max(abs(rot_translated - rot_original)) > rot_tol or abs(rms_translated - rms_original) > rms_tol; float64 rot_tol = 1e-6*(1+s), rms_tol = max(1e-6*(s+|t|), max(1e-3, 16*sqrt(eps))*R), R = largest RMS distance of a centred point set from its centroid; for float32 input additionally rot_tol = max(rot_tol, 256*eps*(1+s)) and rms_tol = max(rms_tol, 16*sqrt(eps)*(1+s)), eps = machine epsilon of the coarsest input dtype
checkers.invariant: translating both point sets by the same constant vector t before set()/run() does not change the fitted rotation, and changes the RMSD by no more than the numerical-error budget of the centering subtraction, since run() explicitly mean-centers both point sets before fitting
checkers.observation_point: a probe re-running set()/run() on (reference_coords + t, coords + t) and comparing rot/rms against the untranslated fit
checkers.precondition: any two point sets of equal size N >= 3 with matching shape (Nx3), each spanning a genuine non-collinear/non-coincident configuration, and any additive translation vector t with |t| within the coordinate-magnitude range the caller's point sets already occupy
checkers.rationale: a rigid superposition is a property of relative geometry, not absolute position; if a common translation changes the fitted rotation or RMSD beyond float64 rounding from centroid subtraction, QCP's centering is not actually removing translational degrees of freedom, so structures loaded at different absolute coordinate offsets would silently disagree
checkers.scientific_quantity: optimal rigid-body rotation and its RMSD

checkers.alarm: result < min(self[c] for c in contributing_codons) - tol or result > max(self[c] for c in contributing_codons) + tol, tol = C*eps64*cai_length*scale
checkers.invariant: the returned CAI is a geometric mean of the table weights over the contributing codons, and a geometric mean can never fall outside [min(w_codon), max(w_codon)] over those same codons
checkers.observation_point: in CodonAdaptationIndex.calculate, immediately before returning result
checkers.precondition: any in-frame DNA coding sequence whose codons are all either present in the CodonAdaptationIndex table, ATG/TGG, or a stop codon, with at least one codon contributing to cai_length
checkers.rationale: CAI is defined as a geometric mean of codon-usage weights; a geometric mean of a finite set of positive numbers is bounded by the smallest and largest of those numbers regardless of composition, so a reported value outside that envelope indicates the length-normalization or log/exp aggregation is wrong
checkers.scientific_quantity: codon adaptation index (CAI) as a geometric mean of per-codon relative adaptiveness weights

checkers.alarm: abs(ln(CAI(A+B)) - (L_A*ln(CAI(A)) + L_B*ln(CAI(B)))/(L_A+L_B)) > tol, tol = C*eps64*(L_A+L_B)
checkers.invariant: CAI(A+B) == exp((L_A*ln(CAI(A)) + L_B*ln(CAI(B))) / (L_A+L_B)), where L_A, L_B are each sub-sequence's contributing-codon counts
checkers.observation_point: a probe calling calculate() on A, on B, and on A+B under the same CodonAdaptationIndex instance
checkers.precondition: any two in-frame DNA coding sequences A and B, each producing a numeric CAI with cai_length(A) >= 1 and cai_length(B) >= 1, whose concatenation A+B is also valid under the same table
checkers.rationale: codon boundaries are exactly preserved across concatenation of two in-frame sequences, so the log-mean of the whole must equal the length-weighted average of the log-means of the parts; a violation means calculate() is not a per-codon-independent statistic
checkers.scientific_quantity: codon adaptation index as a per-codon geometric mean, decomposed additively in log-space across a sequence concatenation

checkers.alarm: calculate(S_prime) < calculate(S) - tol, tol = C*eps64*cai_length(S)*scale
checkers.invariant: CAI(S') >= CAI(S), because CAI is exp(arithmetic mean of log-weights) and replacing one term by a term of equal or greater value cannot decrease the mean
checkers.observation_point: a probe calling calculate() on S and on S'
checkers.precondition: any in-frame coding sequence S with at least one contributing codon at some position i, and any synonymous substitution of the codon at position i by a different codon c' encoding the same amino acid with self[c'] >= self[codon_i], producing S' identical to S except at position i
checkers.rationale: CAI is defined so that more highly preferred codons score at least as well as less-preferred synonyms at the same position; a substitution to an equally- or more-preferred synonym that lowers the index means the metric no longer orders sequences consistently with its own definition of codon preference
checkers.scientific_quantity: codon adaptation index as a monotonic function of each contributing codon's table weight

checkers.alarm: for some ATG or TGG codon c present in the sequence, self.get(c) is missing or |self.get(c) - 1.0| > 1e-9
checkers.invariant: whenever calculate() takes the ATG/TGG forced-weight branch for a codon c, the table weight this instance actually computed for c (self.get(c)) must equal 1.0 -- the only condition under which the class's own construction (self[codon] = counts[codon]/max(counts of the same amino-acid group)) guarantees that weight
checkers.observation_point: in CodonAdaptationIndex.calculate, at the point the 'if codon in ["ATG","TGG"]: continue' branch is taken; reconstructed after calculate() returns from the sequence and the already-built index
checkers.precondition: any CodonAdaptationIndex instance constructed via __init__ from any Bio.Data.CodonTable.CodonTable-conforming table whose weights have not been edited since construction, and any in-frame DNA sequence over ACGT containing at least one ATG or TGG codon
checkers.rationale: the exclusion is a numerical shortcut standing in for a fact about the genetic code (Met/Trp encoded by a single codon each); several genetic codes Biopython ships reassign codons so Trp has two synonyms (e.g. TGA reassigned to Trp in several mitochondrial codes, making it synonymous with TGG). Under such a table the shortcut silently forces a codon that may be poorly represented in the reference set to score as if optimally adapted, producing a CAI that is not the geometric mean of this table's own weights
checkers.scientific_quantity: codon adaptation index as a geometric mean of per-codon relative adaptiveness weights derived from the genetic-code table the instance was built with

checkers.alarm: a codon in the sequence is a member of index._table.stop_codons but absent from self, OR a codon is a literal member of {TGA, TAA, TAG}, absent from self, and not a member of index._table.stop_codons
checkers.invariant: any codon that reaches calculate()'s KeyError-and-skip branch must be a true member of index._table.stop_codons for this instance, and conversely no codon in index._table.stop_codons should be absent from self in the first place, since __init__ seeds table.stop_codons as its own synonymous group during construction
checkers.observation_point: in CodonAdaptationIndex.calculate, at the point self[codon] would raise KeyError and the codon is checked against the literal {TGA, TAA, TAG} set; reconstructed after calculate() returns from the sequence, the index, and index._table
checkers.precondition: any CodonAdaptationIndex instance constructed via __init__ from any Bio.Data.CodonTable.CodonTable-conforming table, and any in-frame DNA sequence over ACGT containing at least one codon in the literal set {TGA, TAA, TAG} or in index._table.stop_codons
checkers.rationale: the hardcoded literal set is a shortcut standing in for the table's own declared stop-codon set; several codon tables Biopython ships assign additional or different stop codons (vertebrate mitochondrial stops on AGA/AGG in addition to TAA/TAG), so a coding sequence built under such a table could in principle contain a true stop codon calculate() does not recognize as one
checkers.scientific_quantity: codon adaptation index as a geometric mean restricted to codons that genuinely contribute a synonymous-codon-usage signal under the genetic code the instance was built with

checkers.alarm: the codon about to cause TypeError is present in index._table.forward_table (a genuine sense codon under the instance's declared genetic code) yet absent from index itself
checkers.invariant: for a self-consistent instance, every codon in index._table.forward_table is a key of index (guaranteed jointly by __init__'s construction of self from table.forward_table.items()), so the TypeError branch should never fire for a codon the instance's own table calls a sense codon
checkers.observation_point: inside calculate()'s accumulation loop, in the except KeyError: branch, immediately before raising TypeError
checkers.precondition: any CodonAdaptationIndex instance and any in-frame DNA sequence over {A,C,G,T}, observed at the moment calculate() is about to raise TypeError for a codon unresolved by self and not in the literal stop set {TGA,TAA,TAG}
checkers.rationale: an index that reports a codon as illegal, when its own declared genetic code recognizes that codon as coding for an amino acid, means the weight table and the genetic-code declaration carried by the same instance have drifted apart
checkers.scientific_quantity: sense/stop codon partition under the instance's own genetic code table

checkers.alarm: the observed weight is not in the interval (0, 1 + 1e-9]
checkers.invariant: 0 < self[codon] <= 1 for every codon calculate() looks up, as a direct consequence of __init__'s counts[codon] >= 0.5 pseudo-count floor and denominator = max(counts[c] for c in synonymous group) >= counts[codon]
checkers.observation_point: inside calculate()'s accumulation loop, immediately after a successful self[codon] lookup and before log(weight) is evaluated
checkers.precondition: any CodonAdaptationIndex instance built via __init__ (any training-sequence iterable, any genetic-code table) and any in-frame DNA sequence accepted by calculate, observed at each codon actually looked up in the accumulation loop
checkers.rationale: a weight outside (0,1] contradicts the constructive definition of w_ij that __init__ itself guarantees; either log() aborts the calculation with a ValueError never surfaced to any checker, or an out-of-range weight silently pulls the reported index outside the interval the paper's definition guarantees
checkers.scientific_quantity: Sharp & Li relative synonymous codon-usage weight w_ij
